body:
---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-SDK-CATALOG-PROJECTION-METHOD"
  title: "Catalog: add the authority-fact projection method (blocks the MCP surface in rigorix-oss)"
  epic: "consequence gating / contract"
  component: "API Catalog"
  module: "api-catalog"
  status: planned
  priority: medium
  dependencies:
    - "rigorix-oss ISSUE-PROJECTION-SURFACES (the consumer; filed there)"
    - "rigorix-oss ISSUE-AUTHORITY-FACT-PROJECTION (#1001) — the artifact exists"

  intent: |
    Add a catalog method exposing the authority-fact projection, so rigorix-oss can
    expose it over the governed MCP/HTTP surface. This must land FIRST: a verifier
    or client built against the current catalog will not accept an unknown method,
    so OSS cannot ship the tool ahead of this without breaking parity.

  in_scope:
    - "schemas/api/catalog.json: the canonical method entry (name, params, result, auth level)"
    - "The two polyglot schema copies (python/…/_schemas/api, typescript/_schemas/api)"
    - "rust/rigorix-schemas embedded schema"
    - "rust/rigorix-client catalog + tests"
    - "typescript-client catalog + tests"
    - "go/client catalog_drift_test.go expectations"
    - "schemas/api/method-catalog.md note if it records the set"

  out_of_scope:
    - "Implementing the tool in rigorix-oss (separate issue, that repo)"
    - "Enterprise ingestion/console (separate issue, that repo)"
    - "The projection's own artifact shape — it is not a catalog method result; the \
       result is the existing AuthorityFactBundle JSON (spec §4.3)"

  affected_layers:
    domain:
      - "No change"
    application:
      - "No change"
    infrastructure:
      - "Modified: schema files (canonical + copies) and the embedded schema"
    api:
      - "New: one catalog method; the frozen set grows from 23 to 24"

  canonical_references:
    - module: "schemas/api/catalog.json (the live, frozen method set)"
    - module: "schemas/api/catalog.schema.json"
    - module: "rigorix-oss docs/spec/consequence-gating-v1.md#43-authority-fact-projection-outbound-ours"
    - last_sync: "2026-10-12"

  acceptance_criteria:
    - "The canonical catalog carries the method with params, result schema and auth level"
    - "Both polyglot copies match the canonical catalog byte-for-byte after regeneration"
    - "rust/rigorix-schemas embeds the updated catalog"
    - "rust/rigorix-client + typescript-client + go drift test all agree on the method set"
    - "A minor SDK release is cut; the release notes state the sequencing requirement (consumers must upgrade before the OSS tool ships)"
    - "Verifiers built against the previous release still verify envelopes (additive, no canonical-form break)"

  validators:
    - ci
    - tests
    - architecture
    - canonical

  implementation_notes: |
    ## Sequencing is the whole point

    The 0.3.0 -> 0.4.0 attribution work established the rule: the SDK contract
    lands first, then both servers implement it, then the enterprise mirror follows.
    A consumer built against the old contract either rejects or silently drops the
    new surface. Do not let OSS ship the tool first — the parity tests will fail,
    and that failure is the point.

    ## What a new method actually touches (measured 2026-10-12)

      schemas/api/catalog.json                                canonical, 23 methods
      schemas/api/catalog.schema.json                         the catalog's own schema
      python/rigorix_verifier/_schemas/api/catalog.json        copy
      typescript/_schemas/api/catalog.json                     copy
      rust/rigorix-schemas/src/lib.rs                          embeds the schemas
      rust/rigorix-client/src/catalog.rs + tests/{catalog,protocol}.rs
      typescript-client/test/{catalog,protocol}.test.ts
      go/client/catalog_drift_test.go                          drift test across languages
      schemas/api/method-catalog.md                            historical sketch; catalog.json is authoritative

    ## Is this the right addition at all?

    The catalog is frozen for good reasons, and the projection is an EXPORT for an
    external consumer or an auditor — not a step an agent takes mid-run. Adding a
    method widens the agent-visible surface for something fundamentally offline.

    The alternative is to keep the projection CLI-only (it is already reachable
    that way once rigorix-oss ISSUE-PROJECTION-SURFACES lands) and never touch the
    catalog. That may well be the better answer.

    **Do not implement this issue until that question is answered.** It is filed so
    the cost is visible and the decision is explicit, not so it is assumed. If the
    answer is "CLI only", close it.

    ## Additive-only

    If it proceeds: the method is additive. Old verifiers must still verify
    envelopes; nothing in the canonical (HMAC) form of an envelope may change. The
    projection is a separate artifact (spec §4.3), not an envelope field.

  file_changes:
    - "modify: schemas/api/catalog.json"
    - "modify: python/rigorix_verifier/_schemas/api/catalog.json"
    - "modify: typescript/_schemas/api/catalog.json"
    - "modify: rust/rigorix-schemas/src/lib.rs (embedded schema)"
    - "modify: rust/rigorix-client/src/catalog.rs"
    - "modify: rust/rigorix-client/tests/catalog.rs"
    - "modify: typescript-client (catalog test)"
    - "modify: go/client/catalog_drift_test.go"

  pipeline_steps:
    - implement
    - validate
    - create-mr
    - merge
---

# ISSUE-SDK-CATALOG-PROJECTION-METHOD

## Intent

`rigorix-oss` wants an MCP tool exposing the authority-fact projection
(`ISSUE-PROJECTION-SURFACES`). The governed surface is driven by the frozen
catalog in this repo, so **the catalog change lands here first** — OSS cannot ship
the tool ahead of it without breaking parity.

## Read this before implementing

**This issue should not be started until the question below is answered.** It is
filed to make the cost visible, not to presume the outcome.

> Is an MCP tool the right surface for the projection at all?

The projection is an export for an external determination consumer or an auditor.
It is fundamentally an offline artifact, not a step an agent takes mid-run.
Keeping it CLI-only avoids a three-repo contract change and does not widen the
agent-visible surface. **If the answer is "CLI only", close this issue.**

If it proceeds, the artifact remains the `AuthorityFactBundle` JSON from spec §4.3 —
this issue adds a method that returns it, not a new artifact shape.

## Sequencing (the reason this is a separate issue)

```
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ THIS ISSUE — SDK catalog    │  1. canonical + copies + clients + drift test
│ method (minor release)      │     must land and ship FIRST
└──────────────┬──────────────┘
               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ rigorix-oss                 │  2. mcp descriptor + routing + server parity
│ ISSUE-PROJECTION-SURFACES   │
└──────────────┬──────────────┘
               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ rigorix-enterprise          │  3. ingestion + console
└─────────────────────────────┘
```

A consumer built against the current catalog will not accept an unknown method.
This is the same ordering rule the 0.3.0 → 0.4.0 attribution release established.

## What a new method touches (measured)

| artifact | role |
|---|---|
| `schemas/api/catalog.json` | canonical, 23 methods |
| `schemas/api/catalog.schema.json` | the catalog's own schema |
| `python/rigorix_verifier/_schemas/api/catalog.json` | copy |
| `typescript/_schemas/api/catalog.json` | copy |
| `rust/rigorix-schemas/src/lib.rs` | embeds the schemas |
| `rust/rigorix-client/src/catalog.rs` + `tests/` | client + parity |
| `typescript-client/test/` | client parity |
| `go/client/catalog_drift_test.go` | cross-language drift test |

## Acceptance Criteria

| # | Criterion | Validator |
|---|-----------|-----------|
| 1 | Canonical catalog carries the method (params, result, auth level) | `validate-canonical.sh` |
| 2 | Both polyglot copies match the canonical byte-for-byte | `validate-ci.sh` |
| 3 | `rigorix-schemas` embeds the updated catalog | `validate-tests.sh` |
| 4 | rust/ts/go clients + drift test agree on the method set | `validate-tests.sh` |
| 5 | Minor release shipped; notes state consumers must upgrade before OSS ships | review |
| 6 | Additive only — old verifiers still verify envelopes | `validate-tests.sh` |

## Implementation

> **Agent:** Confirm the surface decision first. If the answer is CLI-only, stop and
> close this issue. If it proceeds, the canonical catalog is edited first and every
> copy is regenerated from it — never hand-edited in parallel.

### Steps

1. Confirm the surface decision (MCP tool vs CLI-only)
2. Add the method to `schemas/api/catalog.json` (name, params, result, auth level)
3. Regenerate the python/typescript copies and the embedded schema
4. Update `rigorix-client`, `typescript-client` and the go drift test
5. Verify an old verifier still verifies envelopes (additive)
6. Cut a minor release; state the sequencing requirement in the notes
title: Catalog: add the authority-fact projection method (blocks the MCP surface in rigorix-oss)

body:
---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-SDK-VALIDATOR-MAINTENANCE"
  title: "Rust validators carry a latent false-failure (cargo test --test '*') and have diverged from the OSS copies"
  epic: "tooling / ci integrity"
  component: "CI / Validators"
  module: "validator-tooling"
  status: planned
  priority: medium
  dependencies:
    - "rigorix-oss ISSUE-VALIDATOR-SINGLE-SOURCE (the counterpart, filed there)"

  intent: |
    Two defects in the SDK's rust validators: (1) a latent false failure —
    `cargo test --test '*'` errors on any target declaring `required-features`, so
    the validator will report a test failure the moment such a target is added;
    and (2) divergence — the same filenames exist in rigorix-oss with different
    content, so "run validate-tests" means different things in the two repos.

  in_scope:
    - "Replace `cargo test --test '*'` with `cargo test --tests` in the rust validators"
    - "Decide and record the source of truth for validator scripts shared with rigorix-oss"
    - "Fix the hardcoded 'language: C.UTF-8' message if present in this repo's dispatchers"

  out_of_scope:
    - "Reconciling the intra-repo trees (this repo has no per-crate mirrors)"
    - "Changing the validation semantics themselves"

  affected_layers:
    domain:
      - "No code change"
    application:
      - "No code change"
    infrastructure:
      - "Modified: .pi/scripts/languages/rust/validate-tests.sh"
      - "Modified: .pi/scripts/languages/rust/validate-integration.sh"
      - "Modified possibly: .pi/scripts/validate-*.sh (the locale message)"

  canonical_references:
    - module: "rigorix-oss docs/issues/validator-single-source.md (counterpart issue)"
    - last_sync: "2026-10-12"

  acceptance_criteria:
    - "No `.pi/scripts/languages/rust/*.sh` uses `cargo test --test '*'`"
    - "A target declaring required-features does not produce a false failure"
    - "The validator still runs the real test suite when a required-features target is present"
    - "The source-of-truth relationship with the rigorix-oss copies is recorded, not implicit"
    - "validate-ci.sh passes"

  validators:
    - ci
    - tests

  implementation_notes: |
    ## Why `--test '*'` is wrong

    `cargo test --test '*'` explicitly selects every test target. If ANY of them
    declares `required-features` that are not enabled, cargo ERRORS rather than
    skipping — so the validator reports a test failure that has nothing to do with
    the tests. `cargo test --tests` is the same intent but skips such targets.

    This was hit for real in rigorix-oss (engine's `conformance` target declares
    `required-features`): `--test '*'` exited 101, `--tests` exited 0. It is latent
    here only because rigorix-sdk has no `required-features` target TODAY —
    verified 2026-10-12. Adding one turns this into an immediate false failure.

    Current lines:

        .pi/scripts/languages/rust/validate-tests.sh:70       cargo test --test '*' --quiet
        .pi/scripts/languages/rust/validate-integration.sh:45 cargo test --test '*' --quiet

    ## Divergence from rigorix-oss

    Measured 2026-10-12 — all seven `languages/rust/validate-*.sh` files differ
    between the two repos:

      validate-architecture   OSS 9b3fb4  SDK 8c8f54
      validate-canonical      OSS 578366  SDK 57aa99
      validate-ci             OSS 488f33  SDK 190560
      validate-integration    OSS 7200e2  SDK 1c1fd6
      validate-tests          OSS e05dd6  SDK 03a5f1
      validate-security       OSS 19e950  SDK 490a4f
      validate-operations     OSS a46327  SDK ab8972

    Note the SDK and OSS are ALSO internally inconsistent in different ways: the
    SDK's `validate-tests.sh` already uses `cargo llvm-cov` (the newer coverage
    tool) while still carrying `--test '*'` (the older defect); OSS has the
    reverse mixture in places. So this is not "one repo is behind" — the two trees
    have been edited independently.

    Recommendation: pick one repo as the source of truth and make the other fetch
    or generate, OR accept divergence and record an explicit compatibility note.
    Either is fine; leaving it implicit is not.

  file_changes:
    - "modify: .pi/scripts/languages/rust/validate-tests.sh"
    - "modify: .pi/scripts/languages/rust/validate-integration.sh"
    - "modify: .pi/scripts/validate-*.sh (the locale message, if present)"

  pipeline_steps:
    - implement
    - validate
    - create-mr
    - merge
---

# ISSUE-SDK-VALIDATOR-MAINTENANCE — a latent false failure, and divergence from OSS

## 1. `cargo test --test '*'` is a latent false failure

```bash
.pi/scripts/languages/rust/validate-tests.sh:70        if cargo test --test '*' --quiet
.pi/scripts/languages/rust/validate-integration.sh:45  if cargo test --test '*' --quiet
```

`--test '*'` selects every test target explicitly. If any target declares
`required-features` that are not enabled, cargo **errors** instead of skipping, and
the validator reports a failure unrelated to the tests.

This happened for real in `rigorix-oss`:

| command | result on a target with `required-features` |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --test '*'` | **exit 101** (error) |
| `cargo test --tests` | **exit 0** (target skipped) |

**Latent here, not benign.** Verified 2026-10-12: this repo currently has **no**
`required-features` target, so nothing fails today. Adding one — which the
conformance/feature-gated pattern makes likely — turns it into an immediate false
failure. The fix is one token.

## 2. Divergence from `rigorix-oss`

All seven `languages/rust/validate-*.sh` differ between the repos (hashes in the
implementation notes). Neither is uniformly newer: this repo already uses
`cargo llvm-cov` while still carrying `--test '*'`; OSS has the inverse mixture in
places. They have simply been edited independently.

That matters because the filenames and command names are identical, so
"`validate-tests` passed" does not mean the same thing in the two repos.

## Acceptance Criteria

| # | Criterion | Validator |
|---|-----------|-----------|
| 1 | No rust validator uses `--test '*'` | `validate-ci.sh` |
| 2 | A `required-features` target does not cause a false failure | `validate-tests.sh` |
| 3 | Source-of-truth relationship with the OSS copies is recorded | review |
| 4 | The `C.UTF-8` message is fixed if present here | `validate-ci.sh` |

## Implementation

> **Agent:** Step 1 is a one-token fix and can land alone. Step 3 is a decision
> (shared source vs recorded divergence) — do not silently copy files across repos.

### Steps

1. Replace `--test '*'` with `--tests` in both validators
2. Verify: with a temporary `required-features` target, the validator passes and the suite still runs
3. Decide the source-of-truth relationship with rigorix-oss and record it
4. Fix the locale message if present
5. Run `validate-ci.sh`
title: Rust validators carry a latent false-failure (cargo test --test '*') and have diverged from the OSS copies
